transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my mind just feels... foggy. I work at the library, and lately I can't even keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. It's frustrating. I just sit there and I can't even seem to decide what simple thing to do next.
Have you noticed any memory problems or confusion lately, like forgetting things you’d normally remember or getting lost in familiar places?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been getting lost or forgetting important things, really. It's not like my memory is gone. It's more just... I can't seem to focus or make a decision. The information is in my head, I just can't seem to organize it or figure out what to do with it.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table and it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. I usually enjoy going through my old watercolor books, but now... opening them just makes me feel heavy instead of interested. I don't really have the desire to do much of anything.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally demanding?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I sit around a lot more right now, but it's not because my body is exhausted. I'm not physically tired... my energy levels are mostly fine. It's just that heavy feeling I mentioned. I guess I have the energy, I just don't have the drive to do anything with it.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down or that you’re moving more slowly than usual, like everything is in slow motion?

Yeah, I have noticed that. My body just feels slow lately. It's like... even just walking to the corner store, or trying to sort through papers on my desk at work, it all takes way more effort than it should. Everything just feels heavier and slower.
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re failing at things you should be able to handle?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm not getting as much done, but I don't sit around feeling worthless or like a failure. I don't really beat myself up over it. I know I can handle my job at the library and my day-to-day life, it's just... I just don't have the drive right now. So no, I haven't been feeling bad about myself in that way.
Have you noticed any trouble with thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?

Yeah, actually, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. My mind just feels really foggy. It's like I can't think clearly at all. At the library, I can't even keep my place when I'm looking at my old cataloging notes, which is usually second nature to me. And making decisions... even just trying to figure out what simple thing I should do next takes forever. I just can't seem to focus.
Do these feelings of mental fog, slowed thinking, and lack of drive happen most of the time, even outside of work at the library, like at home or when you're out with friends?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really paid attention to whether it's happening all the time at home. And... well, I don't really go out with friends much anyway, so I couldn't tell you about that. I just know I notice it the most when I actually have to get a task done.
How long have you been feeling this way with the mental fog, slowed thinking, and lack of drive?

Well, I'd say it's been going on for about three months now. That's when I really started noticing it, anyway. It was right around the time I started getting things ready to leave my job at the library. It's been pretty much most days since then that I've just felt this... fogginess and lack of drive.
Have you found it hard to concentrate on things, even simple tasks, because your mind feels foggy or unclear?

Yeah, exactly like I was saying a minute ago. It really is. Even the simple stuff... it just takes forever to figure out. I sit there and try to focus on what I'm supposed to be doing, but that fog just gets in the way of getting much of anything done.
Have you noticed that things that used to give you pleasure, like your hobbies or spending time with loved ones, don’t seem to bring you any joy or satisfaction anymore?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table and it feels like... I don't know, like the color has just gone out of everything. I used to really like painting with my old watercolor books, but now when I look at them, I don't feel interested at all. They just make me feel heavy. So, no, I'm not really getting any joy out of the things I used to like.
